hints.content:
$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)$ represents the value $f$ approaches as $x$ becomes infinitely negative (i.e., as we move on the graph to the left).

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ represents the value $f$ approaches as $x$ becomes infinitely positive (i.e., as we move on the graph to the right).

![The graph of function f has the first curve approaching the horizontal asymptote y = negative 5 as x approaches negative infinity. The second curve approaches the horizontal asymptote y = 3 as x approaches positive infinity.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/81eea607d46edf8356de9be64fe2bf2fb0733906)

$\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)$ seems to approach $-5$ and $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)$ seems to approach $3$.

In conclusion, these are the limits of $f$ at negative and positive infinity:

$\begin{align}
&\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-\infty}f(x)=-5
\\\\
&\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}f(x)=3
\end{align}$
